name: Single-Arm Supinated Pulldown
grip: Supinated (underhand) grip on D-handle with palm facing inward/backward.
description: Pull a high cable D-handle downward with a supinated grip to the upper chest, aligning elbow path with latissimus fibers while seated.
setup: Attach a single D-handle to an overhead cable pulley and adjust the thigh pads to secure your legs.
Sit tall on the bench, sliding thighs snugly under the pads with feet flat on the floor.
Reach overhead with working arm and grasp D-handle with a supinated (underhand) grip, allowing arm to fully extend.
Rest non-working hand on thigh pad or bench for stability.
instructions: Initiate the pull by drawing the elbow down and slightly inward toward your hip.
Keep torso tall with a slight natural thoracic arch, avoiding twisting or leaning sideways.
Pull until the handle approaches collarbone or upper chest level, achieving a strong contraction in the lat.
Control the return upward until the working arm is fully extended overhead and the lat is stretched.
Complete all repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
cues: Drive elbow down to your hip.
commonMistakes: Twisting or leaning the torso laterally to yank the handle down.
Using an overhand grip instead of supinated, altering the pulling plane.
Failing to secure thighs under pads.
